PayRight — evidence

Every invoice below went through the live Sarvam Document AI reader (advanced mode) and our real check.py. We generated each invoice ourselves, so we know what is truly printed on it and can score the reader field by field. Nothing here is typed in by hand. The "handwritten" bills are generated pages in a handwriting font made to look like phone photos. One real handwritten bill (team photo, private details blacked out) is in payright/test_sets/real/, waiting to be read.

23
languages read: 22 Indian languages + English
7/7
planted traps caught before any money moved
22/34
genuine bills cleared to pay; not paid: 10 asked about, 2 stopped
0
wrong payments approved across 41 invoices
96%
of 410 critical fields read exactly right
98%
of 123 money fields (total, account, IFSC) read right
30/41
invoices got an accepted decision

Not read yet: inv09_hope.png (made and in the answer key, waiting for Sarvam credits). Not counted above.

What these tests taught us

  • On an unreadable photo the reader invents data. On lad4 Sarvam returned account 0123456789012345, a GSTIN and a 2023 date that are not on the bill. It scored that account 0 confidence, but our reader treated a 0 as fully sure (0 or 1 is 1 in Python). We fixed it: a 0 now marks the field unsure. The bill was never at risk, because code compares every account with the one on file.
  • A model reads, code decides, and that is why it held. Every wrong read we saw was caught by a cross-check (account on file, GSTIN, arithmetic, amount in words), not by trusting the model's confidence.
  • Scripts are not the hard part. Tamil and Hindi names, Tamil and Hindi amounts in words, Devanagari digits and lakh notation were all read right. On Devanagari digits Sarvam was unsure (0.5) of a correct total, so the owner is asked once instead of the bill being paid on a guess.
  • One systematic slip: the letter O inside Hope's GSTIN is read as zero on every Hope bill. Usually harmless, since the vendor is then matched by name, but it is why the GSTIN is never the only key.
  • All 22 Indian languages read. Across the 20-language set Sarvam read 193 of 200 critical fields right, and every total, account number and IFSC in every language. But it scores non-English vendor names at 0.5 confidence, so 9 clean bills are asked about rather than paid. Measured fix for the checker: do not ask about the name when the GSTIN or the account on file already proves the vendor. On our saved reads that turns those 9 into PAY and changes nothing else in all 41 invoices. The Assamese bill was stopped (safely) because the GSTIN slip and an Assamese name with no English reading left the vendor unidentified; an Assamese alias in the vendor list, or reading O and 0 alike in a GSTIN, would fix it.
